caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The bar chart compares per-output and per-layer perplexity across different sparsity rates, with the x-axis representing sparsity rate in percentage increments from 10% to 80% and the y-axis showing perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. Each sparsity rate has two grouped bars: a blue bar for per-output and an orange bar for per-layer. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate from left to right. At sparsity rates of 10% to 50%, both configurations show low perplexity values, with per-output and per-layer values remaining below 10^1. At 60% sparsity, the per-output perplexity is approximately 15 while per-layer remains near 10^1. At 70% sparsity, per-output perplexity increases to around 50, while per-layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with per-output exhibiting slightly higher values than per-layer. The legend identifies the blue bars as "Per-Output" and the orange bars as "Per-Layer."
